texts.facts: Dated this the 21st day of May, 2020. The revision petitioner is aggrieved by the conviction and sentence imposed on him by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kochi for the offence under Section 16 (1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50 (1) of the PFA Rules, as affirmed in appeal by the Additional Sessions Court, (Ad hoc-I), Ernakulam. 2. The revision petitioner was conducting an ice cream parlour in Chellanam Grama Panchayat. On 7.12.1998, the Food Inspector, Kochi Circle conducted an inspection during the course of which, 1 litre of cow milk was purchased from the parlour, which, on analysis, was found to be adulterated. The Food Inspector found that as on the date of inspection, the icecream parlour was being conducted without valid licence as mandated under the PFA Act and Rules. Thereupon, a complaint was filed by the Food Inspector, arraying the petitioner as the first accused, the nominee of the milk manufacturing company as the second accused and the company as the third accused. The offences alleged were under sections 2(ia) (a) (m), 7(iii), 17 r/w 16 (1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50 (1) of the PFA Rules. The appeal filed by the petitioner against the conviction and sentence having been dismissed, this revision petition is filed challenging the judgments of the trial and appellate courts.
texts.arguments: 4. Sri.Santhosh Subrahmanian, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner made elaborate and authoritative submissions on the various aspects of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the Rules thereunder, which now stands repealed and replaced by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Though attempt was made to assail the conviction contending that the provisions of the Panchayat Raj Act would come to the rescue of the revision petitioner, the learned counsel was fair enough to submit that the provisions of the PFA Act, which is a central legislation would prevail over the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, a state enactment. The contention was therefore essentially confined to the quantum of sentence imposed, which is simple imprisonment for three months. 5. The penalty provision with respect to sale of article of food without licence falls under Section 16, the relevant portion of which is extracted hereunder:- "16. (ii) other than an article of food referred to in sub-clause (i), in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or of any rule made thereunder; (b)xx (c)xx (d)xx (e)xx (f)xx (g)xx Provided that - (i) if the offence is under sub-clause (i) of clause (a) and is with respect to an article of food, being primary food, which is adulterated due to human agency or is with respect to an article of food which is misbranded within the meaning of sub-clause (k) of clause (ix) of section 2; or (ii) if the offence is under sub-clause (ii) of clause (a), but not being an offence with respect to the contravention of any rule made under clause (a) or clause (g) of sub-section (1A) of section 23 or under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 24 , the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to two years, and with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees: Provided further that if the offence is under sub-clause (ii) of clause (a) and is with respect to the contravention of any rule made under clause (a) or clause (g) of sub-section (1A) of section 23 or under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 24, the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months Salim A.M. Alias Salim Marshal vs Food Inspector on 21 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183772987/ 3 and with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees." Reading of the provision shows that for offences under Section 17 (1) (a)(ii), with respect to the contravention of any rule made under clause (a) or (g) of Section 23 (1-A), the court may for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine, which may extend to five hundred rupees. But, if the offence under Section 17 (1) (a)(ii is not with respect to any rule made under clause (a) or (g) of Section 23 (1-A), the court may impose a sentence of imprisonment which shall not be less than three months, but which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees. 8. Section 23 deals with the power of the Central Government to make Rules. Sub-section (1-A) of Section 23 specifies the matters which the rules thus framed may provide for. Sub clause(g) of Section 23(1- A) empowers the Government to frame rules defining the conditions of sale or conditions of licence of sale of any article of food.
